bugs.summary: strptime() fails to parse %w of '0' in LC_CTYPE=C
bugs.creator: michaelchirico4

comments.creator: michaelchirico4
comments.text:
Created attachment 3774
Handle %w of '0' consistently in LC_CTYPE=C

r63319 introduced a boundary check for `w_strptime_internal` that was not mirrored in `strptime_internal`, so we get this difference in behavior:

```
LC_CTYPE=C          Rscript -e 'strptime("2026 0 0", "%Y %U %w")'
# [1] NA
LC_CTYPE=en_US.utf8 Rscript -e 'strptime("2026 0 0", "%Y %U %w")'
# [1] "2026-01-04 UTC"
```

comments.creator: michaelchirico4
comments.text: I think this can be closed (r90447)?

comments.creator: suharto_anggono
comments.text:
(In reply to Michael Chirico from comment #0)
> Created attachment 3774
> Handle %w of '0' consistently in LC_CTYPE=C
> 
> r63319 introduced a boundary check for `w_strptime_internal` that was not
> mirrored in `strptime_internal`, so we get this difference in behavior:
> 
> ```
> LC_CTYPE=C          Rscript -e 'strptime("2026 0 0", "%Y %U %w")'
> # [1] NA
> LC_CTYPE=en_US.utf8 Rscript -e 'strptime("2026 0 0", "%Y %U %w")'
> # [1] "2026-01-04 UTC"
> ```

With `%U`, week 1 starts at the first Sunday. So, Sunday of week 0 doesn't exist. In fact,

    strftime("2026-01-04", "%Y %U %w")

gives `"2026 01 0"`.

On the other hand,

    strftime("2026-01-04", "%W")

gives `"00"`.

The added code in `w_strptime_internal`, which is supposed to fix Bug 15195, is wrong.

In the formula, `save_wday - w_offset` part is supposed to mean how many days _ahead of_ `w_offset`.

	  if(tm->tm_yday < 0) tm->tm_yday += 7;

should be

	  if(save_wday - w_offset < 0) tm->tm_yday += 7;

.

Alternatively, discard it entirely, but replace

    save_wday - w_offset

in the formula with

    (save_wday - w_offset + 7) % 7

.

    strptime(paste("2026", c("00", "01"), "0"), "%Y %W %w")

should be one week apart, `2026-01-04` and `2026-01-11`.

Once again, the the change to `w_strptime_internal` in r63319 is wrong and shouldn't be followed by `strptime_internal`. For `%U` and Sunday, `strptime_internal` is already correct. For

    strptime("2026 0 0", "%Y %U %w")

, `NA` result is correct and it is `2026-01-04` that is wrong.

What gives wrong result is `%W` and Sunday (Bug 15195). Similar to what is said by  https://stackoverflow.com/questions/14646406/r-conversion-of-week-number-uk-to-posixct-issue#comment20464275_14646756 , r63319 is a partial fix of the problem. It fixes week number 0, but later weeks are still wrong.

comments.text:
(In reply to Suharto Anggono from comment #3)
> Once again, the the change to `w_strptime_internal` in r63319 is wrong and
> shouldn't be followed by `strptime_internal`. 
.........

Yes, I read your comment #2  and actually did think you were right and Michael Ch and I were wrong ...  but I was busy  (upcoming R Sprint in Birmingham ..),
and then forget / postponed this.
...  and I was hoping you would provide a patch correcting both wrong codes, the
old one (in r63319) for `w_strptime_internal` and the 
new one (in r90447) for `strptime_internal`.  If this was already in your own version of `Rstrptime.h`
You could create the patch attachment with something like

    svn diff src/main/Rstrptime.h > Rstrptime_h.patch

But indeed, your description of the needed changes has really been easily sufficient, too, and I am committing them, i.e., a "simplification" - using auxiliary `int del = save_wday - w_offset;`  of the first of the two alternatives you proposed.
I've changed extended the regression tests in `tests/datetime3.R` as well, now requiring `NA` for invalid cases, and also looking at both %U and %W week numbering schemes.

It needs a bit more tests, also just in case for the "internal" tzone setting.
